summary: Describes a MIB module that sits between high-level policy definitions for Differentiated Services and the detailed per-interface configuration. It provides a way to configure diffserv at a more abstract level than the Differentiated Services MIB.

eli5.summary: Instead of setting each router queue by hand, this lets an operator describe the overall plan once and have the details filled in.

questions: how to configure diffserv via snmp

difference between diffserv mib and config mib
subtitle: A higher-level interface for configuring traffic treatment in Differentiated Services.

tldr.problem: The Differentiated Services MIB (RFC 3289) allows operators to configure per-interface traffic treatment down to the details of individual queues, but operators need a higher level of abstraction to define policies that apply consistently across many interfaces without repeating every detail.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a configuration MIB that sits between high-level policy definitions and the low-level Differentiated Services MIB. It provides template configurations that can be instantiated on multiple interfaces through a template cloning process that reuses policy definitions.
tldr.outcome: Network operators can now define a traffic treatment policy once as a template and apply it to any interface without manually configuring each interface's queues and parameters.

today: RFC 3747 is an Internet Standard. It defines the standard way to manage Differentiated Services traffic treatment templates in SNMP-based network management systems, allowing operators to define policies once and apply them to multiple devices.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This RFC defines the Differentiated Services Configuration MIB (DIFFSERV-CONFIG-MIB), which provides a conceptual layer above the Differentiated Services MIB (RFC 3289). The Differentiated Services MIB operates at the device instance level, managing the queues and traffic treatment on individual interfaces. The Configuration MIB works at a higher level of abstraction, using configuration templates that describe traffic treatment policies.

A template defines a complete traffic treatment configuration that can be applied to any interface on any device. When a template is activated on a specific interface, the system creates a clone of the template with new indexes so the original template remains available for reuse.

This MIB module is designed to work with the Policy-based Management MIB (RFC 3460-related work), but may also be used with simple SNMP operations without that framework.
sections.eli5: Instead of telling each router 'put important traffic in queue 1, normal traffic in queue 2,' you describe the queuing plan once and the system copies it to each router that needs it.

sections.title: Differentiated Services Background
sections.content:
Differentiated Services (diffserv) is a mechanism for applying different levels of service to network traffic. An operator marks packets with a DSCP (Differentiated Services Code Point) value, which routers use to determine how to treat that traffic: which queue it goes into, what priority it gets, how much bandwidth it can use, and whether it should be dropped if the network is congested.

The Differentiated Services MIB (RFC 3289) provides detailed managed objects for configuring this treatment at the instance level: specifying the exact queues, meters, classifiers, and actions for a particular interface and direction. It includes tables for defining classifiers that match traffic, meters that measure it, actions that modify it, queues that buffer it, and schedulers that prioritize it.

However, an operator who wants to apply the same traffic treatment policy to all ingress interfaces on all routers in a network must configure each instance separately, repeating the same queue parameters, DSCP markings, and rate limits many times over.
sections.eli5: In a network, routers sort traffic into different buckets (queues) based on how important it is. Different routers need the same sorting rules, but the old way meant writing out the rules for each router.

sections.title: Configuration MIB Architecture
sections.content:
The DIFFSERV-CONFIG-MIB defines a single table: the diffServConfigTable. Each row in this table represents one traffic treatment configuration template. The key field is diffServConfigId, a human-readable identifier such as EF (Expedited Forwarding) or AF (Assured Forwarding).

Each configuration entry has a diffServConfigStart field that is a row pointer into one of the template tables in the Differentiated Services MIB. The template tables (such as diffServClfrTable for classifiers, diffServMeterTable for meters, diffServActionTable for actions) form a linked chain: each element points to the next via a 'next' pointer, creating a functional datapath that defines the traffic treatment. This is similar to a linked list data structure.

The template itself exists only in the Differentiated Services MIB tables and remains unchanged. When the configuration needs to be activated on an interface, the system does not modify the template itself; instead, it clones the entire chain of template elements, creating new instances with new indexes for the actual interface.
sections.eli5: A configuration is like a blueprint. It lists all the pieces and how they connect. When you need to use it on a real router, you make a copy of the blueprint with new serial numbers for each piece.

sections.title: Template Cloning and Instantiation
sections.content:
When a configuration template is activated on an interface and direction (ingress or egress), the system must clone the template. This process creates a new instance of each element in the template's functional datapath, with new indexes, while preserving all the configuration values.

Cloning is necessary because the indexes in the Differentiated Services MIB tables must be unique across all instances. A literal copy of the template would create index conflicts. The cloning algorithm works as follows: Starting from the template's first element (pointed to by diffServConfigStart), the system reads each element and its configuration. It creates a new element with a fresh index, copies all the parameter values, and updates the 'next' pointer to reference the newly cloned successor element instead of the original template element. It then moves to the next template element and repeats the process until the entire chain has been cloned.

During cloning, the original template is logically locked so that changes made to it mid-clone do not corrupt the instantiation process. When instantiation is complete, all template entries are unlocked and remain available for cloning on another interface.

If a configuration is activated via policy-based management, the policy system handles any error responses. If activated via direct SNMP SET operations, an accurate error response must be returned; if the template has inconsistent values, the SET must fail.
sections.eli5: When you apply a template to a real router, the system walks through the blueprint, makes a copy of each piece with a new label, and hooks them all together the same way the blueprint shows.

sections.title: Configuration Example
sections.content:
Consider a simple scenario: an ingress interface currently has only a counter action that counts all traffic. An operator wants to apply a new policy that classifies traffic into two streams (one matching a specific IP filter, one matching all other traffic), meters each stream, marks it with an appropriate DSCP (EF for Expedited Forwarding, AF for Assured Forwarding), and counts it.

First, the operator creates a template in the DIFFSERV-CONFIG-MIB with id foo and diffServConfigStart pointing to a classifier. In the Differentiated Services MIB, the template chain includes: a classifier element with precedence that matches the IP filter (and another element with lower precedence that matches all), both leading to meter elements; the meters leading to separate mark actions for EF and AF; the mark actions leading to count actions.

To apply this template to interface 3's ingress direction, the operator uses a policy rule or SNMP SET to set diffServDataPathStart.3.1 to point to the cloned template. The system clones every element in the template chain: the classifier elements, the meter elements, the mark actions, and the count actions. The cloned elements get new indexes (perhaps 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) and the next pointers are updated to chain the cloned elements together in the same order as the template.

The original template remains untouched and can be applied to other interfaces.
sections.eli5: You have a recipe that says 'sort traffic three ways, measure it, mark it, and count it.' You apply it to router 3, and the system makes a copy with new serial numbers for each step. Now router 3 follows that exact recipe.

sections.title: Managed Objects
sections.content:
The DIFFSERV-CONFIG-MIB module defines one main table: diffServConfigTable. Each row in this table contains the following objects:

diffServConfigId: A unique identifier string (up to 116 octets) for the configuration template. This allows an operator to reference templates by a meaningful name rather than a numeric index.

diffServConfigDescr: A human-readable description, such as EF or AF, that helps operators identify what behavior the template provides. Management applications can scan this table to find the correct template to apply.

diffServConfigOwner: A string identifying who created this configuration entry, for administrative tracking.

diffServConfigLastChange: A timestamp of when this entry was last modified, allowing operators to audit changes.

diffServConfigStart: A RowPointer that references the starting element of the template's functional datapath. This must point to a valid entry in the Differentiated Services MIB (such as a classifier, meter, action, drop mechanism, or queue).

diffServConfigStorage: Specifies how this configuration is stored (volatile or non-volatile). Entries are recommended to be non-volatile so configurations persist across agent restarts.

diffServConfigStatus: A RowStatus object that allows creation, deletion, and activation of this configuration template.
sections.eli5: Each template record says: here is a name and description for this traffic treatment, who created it, when it was last changed, where the first step of the recipe is, and whether to remember it after the router reboots.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The DIFFSERV-CONFIG-MIB contains several read-create objects that could affect network traffic treatment if modified without authorization.

The diffServConfigDescr, diffServConfigOwner, and diffServConfigStatus objects are not security-sensitive: they do not affect traffic behavior.

However, unauthorized changes to diffServConfigStart could redirect traffic to an unintended configuration, causing packets to receive incorrect priority, marking, or dropping. This could lead to denial of service or unintended behavior.

Similarly, unauthorized changes to diffServConfigStorage could cause configurations to be lost after a router reboot, as some configurations might not be saved if the storage type is volatile.

Additionally, because this MIB instantiates templates from the Differentiated Services MIB, unauthorized changes to those underlying objects could also cause configuration problems. Operators should apply SNMP access control to restrict SET operations on these objects to trusted management stations.

SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 lack adequate security mechanisms. Deployment of SNMPv3 with cryptographic security is strongly recommended. Even with SNMPv3, proper access control lists must be configured to restrict who can modify configuration objects.
sections.eli5: If someone bad can change the router's configuration without permission, they could break your network traffic. You need a password or encryption so only trusted people can change these settings.
